45 Inkerman Street

Caulfield 3162

19/1/2007

Dear Dr.Isaacson,

RE: Mr. Jing Zu

I am writing to refer Mr Zu, a 72-year-old retired school teacher whose features are suggestive of ischemic   Comment [teacher1]: worsening
heart disease.

Mr. Zu has been suffering from hypertension, ischemic heart disease and congestive heart failure for many
years. Accordingly, he has been commenced on Lasix, Arginine, enalapril and nifedipine.                       Comment [teacher2]: a

On 3/1/20117, Mr. Zu firstly presented with angina on exertion which was neither relieved with Arginine
nor resting. His examination was unremarkable apart from hypertension (blood pressure was 160/90) and         Comment [teacher3]: arginine and
bilateral basal crepitations. On 15/1/2007, his condition deteriorated. He came complaining of progressive
dyspnea and orthopnea .His examination revealed lower limb edema up to the knees in addition to chest
crepitations extending to the middle lung zones. Consequently, Lasix dose was increased to 80 mg.

Today, the patient presented with a history of angina episode on mild exertion which lasted for 10 minutes
yesterday. However, his complaint of dyspnea decreased. ECG confirmed anterolateral myocardial
ischemic changes.

In view of the above, I would appreciate if you provide an assessment of Mr Zu and advice regarding           Comment [teacher4]: as well as the
treatment and management his condition as you see suitable. Should you have any queries, please do not        Comment [teacher5]: of
hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor
